title: a stored inferred-fallible result propagated with postfix bang compiles under a matching contract and selects both variants at run time
notes: THE ACCEPTANCE HALF of the binding edge, and the reason it is not merely nice to have: the edge its two refusing siblings pin was added in round 7, and an edge added to make a program REFUSED is one edit away from refusing the program that must be accepted. MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX, this exact shape — store an inferred-fallible call in a local, propagate it with `!`, declare the matching contract — did not compile on the Go fork at all: SMITHERS1302 (a Result the binding is not consuming) plus SMITHERS1207 (the `!` has no Result to propagate), two rules contradicting each other about one value, on the most ordinary store-then-propagate spelling in the language. specification/failures.mdx (Locked): postfix `!` propagates the failure variant to the enclosing Result-returning function; 02-unwrap-propagation/unwrap-returns-the-error-variant pins that for a call written inline and an ANNOTATED callee. The two things this case adds are the local binding and the INFERRED callee, and the second matters because a row that is still being computed is what the reference used to read while deciding whether the propagation existed — so it answered 'plain, no failures' for exactly the callees the rule exists for. BOTH VARIANTS ARE PRINTED. A backend that recognized the propagation but lost the failure would print two success lines; one that lost the success path would not compile. The failure line's identity is minted by the compiler rather than read off the constructor, for the reason conformance/README.md records under 'How an output case is observed'. The refusing halves are 02-unwrap-propagation/a-stored-inferred-fallible-result-charges-the-contract and 02-unwrap-propagation/a-satisfies-wrapped-propagation-charges-the-contract.
